h: Puzzle smarter, then roam the Fine City
p: The best escape room teams have one thing in common: they never stop sharing. Call out every number, colour, letter and symbol you find, and keep found items together so they don't get buried under coats and bags. If you've been staring at the same lock for ages, move on to something else and come back to it later. Escape rooms often have more than one puzzle running at once, so the answer to one might be hiding in another.

Norwich is a university city with a lively student crowd, so expect plenty of groups of mates celebrating birthdays or the end of exams. It's just as popular with families, who find it a great way to get everyone working together for an hour rather than drifting off in different directions.

Once you're out, the city centre is yours to explore. The Norwich Lanes, a maze of independent shops, cafés and pubs, are well worth a wander, and the Art Nouveau Royal Arcade is a beautiful little shortcut through to the market. The Forum, the striking glass building beside St Peter Mancroft church, hosts events and has places to eat. For a quieter stroll, follow the riverside walk along the Wensum past Pull's Ferry, the old water gate near the cathedral, or seek out the hidden Plantation Garden, a Victorian garden tucked into a former chalk quarry. And if you've got time to spare, the Norfolk Broads are only a short drive away, perfect for a day on the water.
